newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD outlines plan to restructure German tax.
newsitem.headline: German SPD outlines plan to restructure German tax.

text.p: Germans opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Monday presented a budget-neutral plan to restructure some 78 billion marks ($46.3 billion) of revenues in the tax system, giving tax breaks to families and workers while raising revenues elsewhere.

SPD chairman Oskar Lafontaine told a news briefing that the partys tax proposals would cut taxes for an average family of four by 2,500 marks per year. The SPD controls the upper house of parliament, the Bundesrat.

He said some 48 billion marks of tax reductions would come through measures including a cut in the basic rate of income tax from 25.9 percent to 15 percent and a reduction in taxes on reinvesting corporate profit from 45 percent to 35 percent.
He added a further 30 billion marks of labour costs would be saved by reducing social payments companies and workers pay by two percenhtage points.

Lafontaine said the tax cuts would be balanced by measures including the cutting of what he called unjustified tax subsidies and tax loopholes currently available in Germany and through so-called eco-taxes such as higher taxes levied on petrol.

Lafontaine repeated that a reduction in the 53-percent tax bracket was only possible if it could be financed elsewhere. He did not specify a new top tax rate. He said governments plans to cut the top tax bracket to 39 percent could not be financed.
